objective: Provide a bounded, deterministic, rollback-safe continuous optimization supervisor that observes verified telemetry, predicts resource actions, validates experimental proposals, deploys approved canaries, monitors outcomes, and automatically rolls back regressions without modifying privileged kernel code.

sources.finding: Linux Pressure Stall Information exposes CPU, memory, and I/O pressure as time-based signals suitable for workload observation and resource-management feedback.
sources.implementation_impact: M244 models bounded pressure and health telemetry as validated inputs to deterministic prediction and safety gating rather than embedding a provider-specific scheduler in kernel space.

sources.finding: Kubernetes documents PSI-derived some and full pressure signals for identifying contention and service degradation.
sources.implementation_impact: M244 retains pressure as a bounded control-plane signal and rejects stale, malformed, over-limit, or unverifiable samples before optimization.

sources.finding: Google SRE describes canary releases as controlled exposure with comparison against a control population and rollback on regression.
sources.implementation_impact: M244 separates proposal, validation, canary deployment, monitoring, and rollback; canary approval remains authority-gated and reversible.

features: bounded telemetry windows with monotonic sequence and policy-generation fencing
deterministic forecast and risk scoring over latency, throughput, pressure, thermal, health, cache, queue, and deadline signals
immutable optimization safety bounds and explicit authority, verified-input, and experimental approval gates
canary/control validation with minimum sample windows and bounded regression thresholds
automatic rollback through M243 generation-fenced adaptive policy rollback
append-only SHA-256 chained optimizer journal with replay and tamper rejection
fail-closed malformed event and telemetry handling
concurrent read-side snapshots with serialized write-side state transitions
no privileged kernel self-modification and no model-output authority

benchmark.interpretation: The static loop is intentionally not an apples-to-apples durability comparison. The durable path includes locking, SHA-256 serialization, append, fdatasync, telemetry retention, and forecast processing. M244 exposes a measured durability and control-plane overhead; it does not claim a speedup. The result motivates batched durability as M245.

qualification_limits: M244 is an isolated userspace continuous-optimization supervisor; it does not alter privileged kernel code or replace the Linux scheduler.
The durable path measured 626334.19 ns per sample in this run versus a 2.04 ns static arithmetic loop; the comparison is not apples-to-apples and is not a performance win.
Batched durability, distributed journal transport, physical accelerators, real model-serving workloads, power sensors, and energy-per-inference measurements remain future qualification work.
No physical GPU/NPU, HBM/VRAM, IOMMU/DMA, vendor driver, accelerator reset, or hardware isolation evidence is present.

Production release remains blocked by independent builder equivalence, operator signing and trusted-key lifecycle, physical accelerator qualification, independent external security review, production PKI/KMS/attestation, live multi-host migration and rollback, and operator-owned CVE response.
